rule.title: Hermetic Test Isolation and Explicit Test Sizing
rule.statement: Tests must be explicitly categorized by size (Small/Unit, Medium/Integration, Large/E2E). Small tests must be hermetic, running in-memory with zero disk, network, or external process access.
rule.rationale: Non-hermetic unit tests that make network calls or rely on external state are flaky, slow down feedback loops, and fail intermittently in CI environments.
rule.implementation_guidance: Small tests execute in milliseconds. Medium tests use local database containers. Large tests run full browser workflows.

forbidden.example: A 'unit test' that makes real HTTP fetch calls to a live external API server.

preferred.example: Small test: pure math chunking test in Vitest (<10ms). Medium test: Supertest + test database (<500ms).

source.evidence_quote: Google classifies tests as Small, Medium, and Large. Small tests must be hermetic: no access to network or disk. Hermetic tests are fast, reliable, and deterministic.

rule.title: Truth-in-Testing: Prohibition of False Concurrency Claims on In-Memory Fakes
rule.statement: Pull requests and walkthrough documentation must never claim concurrency locking or race-condition verification based solely on in-memory fake repositories. If a test runs on an in-memory double without real engine locks, the report must state that runtime concurrency is unverified.
rule.rationale: In-memory fakes lack database row locking and transaction serialization. Claiming concurrency safety based on in-memory tests creates false confidence and causes lost-update bugs in production.
rule.implementation_guidance: Verify real concurrency against PostgreSQL using Testcontainers (TEST-INT-001). If using an in-memory test double, explicitly declare 'Domain business logic verified; runtime concurrency unverified'.

forbidden.example: Writing '// Simulates SELECT ... FOR UPDATE' in an in-memory Map and claiming 'Pessimistic Row Locking verified' in the PR summary.

preferred.example: Integration test running concurrent transactions against a real PostgreSQL instance assert that serializable or row-level locks prevent lost updates.

source.book_title: Unit Testing Principles, Practices, and Patterns
source.evidence_quote: Faking or mocking out the database in integration tests is an anti-pattern. You must test against the real database engine because in-memory mocks do not replicate transactional and concurrency semantics.

rule.title: Mandatory Concurrent Execution Testing for Concurrency and Locking Claims
rule.statement: Any code asserting race-condition prevention, optimistic locking, or pessimistic locking must include at least one automated test executing N concurrent requests via Promise.all asserting exact fulfilled/rejected counts and balance invariant preservation.
rule.rationale: Sequential tests cannot verify mutexes or row locks. Race conditions only manifest when concurrent threads attempt conflicting mutations simultaneously.
rule.implementation_guidance: Execute 10 concurrent transfers with Promise.all on an account with balance sufficient for only 3. Assert fulfilled == 3, rejected == 7, and final balance == initial - 600,000.

forbidden.example: Testing a financial transfer service with only sequential 1-by-1 transfers and declaring it race-condition safe.

preferred.example: const results = await Promise.all(requests); expect(fulfilled.length).toBe(3); expect(rejected.length).toBe(7);

source.evidence_quote: Transactional concurrency mechanisms must be validated with simulated concurrent load tests that deliberately induce conflict and assert invariant preservation.
